description:
'invalid def function head: invalid any value ref'. json.erl has true/6 and false/6. Reproducer: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-otp-json/punch/34_fn_named_true.fz

Part of fz-mue (fz runs OTP's json.erl unchanged). Port and harness: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-otp-json/.

comments.text: Wider than the title (Elixir Parity, 2026-11-20). (1) def unquote(x)(...) fails for every name: these are Elixir's unquote fragments, evaluated in the module body and spliced as quoted code (unquote({:+,[],[1,2]}) becomes 1 + 2; a map is refused as an invalid quoted expression). They reuse sc8.144's definition-time evaluator. (2) Clauses from separate items can't join one function: two item-macro calls each emitting t/1 give 't/1 is already defined', where Elixir accepts them. Same idea as gap (A), an attribute between clauses splitting the group: a function is every clause written for its name/arity anywhere in the module body. json.erl's true/6 and false/6 need both. A page comes first.

Proposal page /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-mue.19.html awaits the user. (1) Build fragments over the definition-time evaluator, as quote do <clause> end run in the module body. (2) A function's clauses join across items, republished the way defoverridable already republishes. Correction: gap (A) is already fixed; written clauses with an attribute or def between them group today. Only clauses from separate items fail to join.

User approved the page's recommended answers 2026-11-24 (asked directly by Elixir Parity): (1) fragments over the definition-time evaluator; (2) clauses join across items, republished as defoverridable does. Building.
